title: KV fragmentation investigation notes (WIP)
content:
Doc purpose
- Log reproduction steps + early measurements for KV cache fragmentation issues contributing to p95/p99 decode spikes + occasional OOM / request shedding.
- This is the scratchpad that feeds the Confluence design doc.

Last updated summary (2026-01-27)
- We can reliably reproduce allocator fragmentation in staging with a mixed-length + churn workload.
- Fragmentation correlates strongly with burst tail latency when the scheduler hits “allocation slow path” (free-list scanning + opportunistic eviction) at decode boundaries.
- Biggest driver seems to be long-lived sequences pinning “middle pages” in KV arena while churned short sequences create many small free segments.
- Under H100 80GB, baseline p99 decode latency spikes 2–4x during bursts once fragmentation ratio > ~0.35 (see metric definition below). Under A100 40GB we hit OOM sooner (less headroom), and eviction churn becomes the dominant effect.

Key definitions (working)
- KV arena: contiguous GPU memory region used to back per-sequence KV pages.
- Page: fixed-size allocation unit for KV blocks (current runtime default: 2MB pages; confirm per model profile).
- Fragmentation ratio (working metric):
  - frag_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_contiguous_bytes / total_free_bytes)
  - Interpretation: 0.0 means all free memory is one contiguous span; 1.0 means free space is maximally fragmented into tiny spans.
- “Slow path alloc”: allocation that requires scanning multiple free-list buckets, splitting spans repeatedly, or invoking eviction/defrag code.

Environment / runtime versions
- Staging cluster: sfo2-stg-gpu (H100 80GB) + iad1-stg-gpu (A100 40GB)
- Runtime:
  - baseline measurements: runtime-1.21.9 (commit 8b3c…; built 2026-01-07)
  - after metrics instrumentation: runtime-1.21.11 + pr-19342 (built 2026-01-12)
- Models used:
  - llama-3.1-70b-instruct (primary)
  - mistral-large-ish (secondary sanity)
- Flags (baseline):
  - kv.cache.enabled=true
  - kv.arena.page_mb=2
  - kv.arena.free_list_buckets=12
  - kv.eviction.enabled=false (unless explicitly noted)
- Observability:
  - tracing: enabled in staging
  - metrics: statsd -> Prometheus -> Grafana “Serving Runtime / Allocator” (WIP panels)

Hypotheses (tracked)
H1: Long-lived sessions (multi-turn chat) create “anchors” that prevent coalescing of adjacent free spans, so short-lived request churn produces many unusable gaps.
- Evidence: arena snapshots show pinned segments scattered through mid-arena and free spans split into < 8MB chunks.

H2: Allocation patterns at decode step boundaries amplify spikes.
- Scheduler has synchronized points where many sequences request additional KV pages at once (esp. during burst ramp), so any allocator slowdown hits many requests simultaneously.
- Evidence: latency spikes coincide with elevated “alloc_scan_steps” and “free_list_search_us” (instrumented in pr-19342) and with a spike in “active_decode_sequences”.

H3: Partial stream cancellations leak “stranded” pages or delay reclamation, worsening fragmentation.
- Evidence: one suspicious case from 2026-01-19 run; later found to be a bug that can cause delayed free on cancellation path (likely addressed in pr-19440, not yet rolled into staging when those runs happened).

H4: Prefix cache interactions make fragmentation worse under mixed workloads (some requests reusing long prefixes, some not).
- Evidence: not confirmed. Needs a controlled A/B (prefix cache on/off) with the same workload generator seed.

Reproduction: workload recipes

Recipe A: Mixed length + churn (best reproduction)
Goal: create persistent long-lived allocations + lots of short-lived create/destroy.

Parameters (default)
- Concurrency: 256 total, ramp 0 -> 256 over 120s
- Mix:
  - 25% long sessions: 12 turns, 1.5k–4k prompt tokens each turn, decode 256 tokens
  - 75% short sessions: 1 turn, 50–400 prompt tokens, decode 64 tokens
- Churn:
  - short sessions have 15% cancel rate during decode (simulate client disconnects)
  - short sessions have jittered inter-arrival (bursty Poisson)
- Duration: 45 minutes

Expected outcome
- Frag ratio gradually increases from ~0.05 to >0.30 after ~15–25 min (H100) depending on cancel rate.
- p99 decode spikes appear once frag ratio > ~0.35 and bursts coincide with alloc requests.

How to run (staging)
1) Deploy runtime canary to 5% of pods (no eviction, no compaction).
2) Use benchmark-lab generator (local) or staging job:
   - benchmark-lab: “fragmentation_workload_generator” (see pr-881)
   - run config: frag_mix_churn_v3.yaml
3) Pin traffic to canary cohort using header:
   - x-redwood-canary: kvfrag-a
4) Capture:
   - allocator snapshot every 60s
   - histograms: decode_step_latency_ms p50/p95/p99
   - counters: kv_alloc_slow_path_total, kv_alloc_scan_steps_total
   - gauge: kv_frag_ratio, kv_free_bytes, kv_largest_free_span_bytes

Recipe B: Long-lived only (control)
- 256 concurrency of long sessions, minimal churn, no cancels.
- Result: frag ratio stays low (~0.05–0.12) and p99 stable. Confirms churn is required.

Recipe C: Short-lived only (control)
- 256 concurrency of short sessions, high churn.
- Result: frag ratio increases but slower; latency spikes smaller; likely because fewer pinned anchors.

Allocator snapshot format (current)
- Snapshot is dumped via debug endpoint /internal/kv/allocator_snapshot (staging only).
- Each snapshot includes:
  - arena_total_bytes
  - arena_used_bytes
  - arena_free_bytes
  - largest_free_span_bytes
  - spans: list of {offset, len, state, seq_id?}
  - free_list buckets summary (count + avg span)

Example snapshots (H100 run 2026-01-16)

T+00:05 (frag stable)
- arena_total_bytes=38.0GB
- used=21.6GB
- free=16.4GB
- largest_free_span=14.9GB
- frag_ratio=1-(14.9/16.4)=0.091
- free_list bucket counts (coarse):
  - [2MB]: 12
  - [4MB]: 9
  - [8MB]: 4
  - [16MB+]: 3

T+00:22 (frag rising)
- arena_total_bytes=38.0GB
- used=24.1GB
- free=13.9GB
- largest_free_span=7.6GB
- frag_ratio=1-(7.6/13.9)=0.453
- notable: many free spans in the 2MB–8MB buckets; very few large spans.
- pinned spans: multiple long-lived sequences holding pages in mid-arena (offsets around 9–22GB).

T+00:26 (first big p99 event)
- frag_ratio=0.48
- kv_alloc_slow_path_total increased sharply (see graph notes below)
- decode p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~620ms for ~90 seconds during a burst ramp.

Observations: metrics + latency correlation
(These are from manual Grafana screenshot notes; dashboard panels still moving around.)

Run: H100 / Recipe A / 45m (2026-01-16)
- decode_step_latency_ms
  - baseline steady: p50 ~35–45ms, p95 ~90–140ms, p99 ~160–220ms
  - during burst events after frag>0.35: p99 ~450–800ms (peak ~1.1s once)
- allocator:
  - kv_frag_ratio climbs to ~0.52 plateau
  - kv_largest_free_span_bytes steadily decays even though kv_free_bytes remains relatively flat (classic fragmentation signature)
  - kv_alloc_scan_steps_total rate increases ~3–6x during spikes
  - kv_alloc_time_us p99 shows a strong leading indicator ~10–20s before decode p99 spikes

Run: A100 / Recipe A / 30m (2026-01-18)
- earlier failure: OOM / forced shedding at ~T+18m when frag_ratio ~0.40 and used bytes ~near high-water.
- allocator free bytes still reported ~2.1GB but largest free span only ~96MB. Several alloc failures despite “free bytes” being non-zero.
- Notes: this is the worst-case for naive “free bytes” based admission control.

Notes on burst-driven behavior
- When arrival rate spikes, more sequences simultaneously request new KV pages, which concentrates allocator pressure.
- The scheduler currently does not coordinate page allocation across sequences (each decode loop hits allocator independently), so allocator slow path multiplies.
- We observed that bursts that happen earlier (frag_ratio < 0.25) do not produce meaningful p99 spikes. Same burst pattern later (frag_ratio > 0.4) does.

Cancellation behavior
- Adding 15% cancel rate increases frag growth rate by ~1.2–1.5x (rough).
- Suspected that cancellations create “holes” that don’t coalesce quickly (or at all if adjacent pinned).
- One run (2026-01-19) showed free bytes increasing but used bytes not decreasing in expected proportion after cancellations. We should re-run after the cancellation fix lands (pr-19440).

Reproduction steps (minimal) for engineers
If you want the fastest local reproduction (not perfectly matching prod):
1) Start single-node runtime with GPU (H100 preferred).
2) Set small arena to accelerate:
   - kv.arena.total_gb=10
   - kv.arena.page_mb=2
3) Run generator with:
   - concurrency 128
   - long:short = 1:3
   - cancel_rate=0.20
4) Poll /internal/kv/allocator_snapshot every 30s.
5) Watch frag_ratio vs decode p99. Expect frag_ratio > 0.35 in 8–15 minutes with these smaller settings.

Early conclusions (tentative)
- Fragmentation is real and reproducible; it is not “just noisy neighbors” or GPU thermal events.
- Tail latency spikes have a clear allocator signature (scan steps/time + largest free span collapse).
- Any solution needs:
  - compaction that is budgeted (time/bytes) to avoid making p99 worse
  - scheduler integration (do not compact at arbitrary points)
  - eviction policy that doesn’t cause correctness issues and doesn’t thrash long-lived paid traffic

Open questions / next experiments
1) Metric definition finalization
- Is frag_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_span / free_bytes) sufficient? Or do we need a percentile-of-span-sizes measure?
- Allison requested we standardize names + units before SRE builds alerts.

2) Prefix cache interaction
- Run Recipe A with prefix cache off vs on, same seed.
- Goal: determine if prefix cache allocations are acting as additional “anchors”.

3) Page size / bucketization sensitivity
- Try page_mb=1 vs 2 vs 4 (if supported) with identical workload.
- Hypothesis: smaller pages reduce internal fragmentation but increase metadata + scanning overhead; net unclear.

4) Scheduler sync point confirmation
- Add tracing spans around “kv_alloc” within decode loop.
- Determine whether spikes correspond to prefill->decode boundary, decode step N, or batch merge points.

5) Admission control / backpressure signal
- Explore whether frag_ratio + largest_free_span can be used as backpressure inputs (Lena to advise).
- Example policy idea: when frag_ratio > X AND alloc_time_p99 > Y, reduce max concurrent decode sequences or force earlier eviction for low tier.

6) Cancellation edge case retest
- Re-run cancellation-heavy scenario after pr-19440 is in staging.
- Verify that “free bytes” and “used bytes” behave consistently after cancellation storms.

Appendix: rough timeline / notes
- 2026-01-06: started collecting allocator snapshots; initial suspicion from SUP-28411 (customer burst p99).
- 2026-01-09: confirmed we can induce fragmentation in staging with mixed lengths.
- 2026-01-12: pr-19342 landed in canary build; allocator counters unblocked correlation work.
- 2026-01-16: first clean H100 run showing p99 spikes aligned with alloc slow path.
- 2026-01-18: A100 run hit OOM with non-zero free bytes due to largest free span collapse.
- 2026-01-19: cancellation anomaly observed; filed follow-up; likely addressed in pr-19440.
- 2026-01-27: consolidated this doc for design review prep; moved “final narrative” to Confluence draft spec.

Notes to self
- Keep raw snapshot files somewhere? Right now they’re scattered in /tmp and Slack uploads. We should put a small sample set in Drive (maybe under serving-runtime/kv-snapshots/).
- Don’t overfit to llama-3.1-70b; we need at least one smaller model to ensure allocator behavior is architecture-agnostic.
- SRE wants a crisp “trigger” recommendation for rollback (frag_ratio threshold alone is insufficient; needs compaction/eviction activity + p99 correlation).
